title: Re-seat a stopped UR3e's tripped CSR50 crash sensor: turn the loose flange to its mark and push it in square
instruction: The collision sensor on the stopped UR3e's wrist has tripped. Reset it by hand: put its flange back home, where the triangle on the flange's rim meets the triangle on the housing, then let go and move your hands clear.
context: A robot fitted with a pneumatic collision sensor stays stopped after each crash until a person resets the sensor, so trials of new programs and learned policies on real arms wait for someone at the cell. Zimmer: "After activation, the compensating flange must be put into the home position by hand" (DDOC00267, sec. 6). Hard part: grip a 12 mm rim under a wider housing on a robot wrist, turn the loose flange the short way to its triangle and push it in square, or it stops on its seat.
setup: Robot-cell bench; coordinates in metres from the bench top, x away from the two bench arms, y to their left. A Universal Robots UR3e (11.2 kg; published DH parameters d1 0.15185, a2 -0.24355, a3 -0.2132, d4 0.13105, d5 0.08535, d6 0.0921) is bolted with its base centre at (0.660, -0.040), stopped and braked at joint angles base -35.9, shoulder -81.8, elbow 133.5, wrist 1 -61.7, wrist 2 92.4, wrist 3 0.0 degrees; its tool flange is at (0.365, 0.017, 0.158). On it is a Zimmer CSR50 pneumatic collision sensor (EN ISO 9409-1 TK 50; 0.66 kg; 71 mm tall; metal housing 79 mm across; metal compensating flange 63 mm across, 12 mm of it below the housing at home, four M6 holes and a 6 mm dowel hole on its face). Its axis points back toward the left bench arm and 10 degrees up; at home the flange's face centre is at (0.310, 0.060, 0.170). A black triangle 8 mm wide and 7 mm tall is marked on the housing's rim (uppermost) and one on the flange's rim; at home they point at each other. The end tool was taken off after the crash to be checked; it is not part of the task. Air at 1 bar through a blue 4 mm hose on an M5 fitting; the sensor's M8 switch cable runs to the robot controller. Tripped start: the flange stands 12.5 mm out (its stop), square to the housing, turned 75 degrees counter-clockwise from the mark as seen facing the flange (lot A) or 75 degrees clockwise (lot B). Bench arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Object jitter 0.
scoring: Score 0 if the flange's triangle never comes within 5 degrees of the housing's (tip to tip 2.7 mm or more on a close photo with a steel rule), for example the flange pushed straight in off the mark (it stops on its seat 2.5 mm out) or turned the long way to its stop; also 0 if the simulation's trial record is incomplete. Touching or bracing on the braked UR3e is allowed. Otherwise the highest row reached. 1.0: at the end the sensor reports ready (its switch input on the robot controller's I/O screen, or an LED on its M8 cable), the flange is home (a 0.5 mm feeler leaf enters the joint nowhere round it; the triangle tips within 1.4 mm, 2.5 degrees), and for the last 1 s both bench grippers, their fingers and their last wrist links stay 20 mm or more from the sensor and the flange does not move (video). 0.75: ready at the end, but a gripper is within 20 mm or that hold is shorter than 1 s. 0.5: at some moment the flange was flush (the largest gap round the joint 1 mm or less) with the triangle tips within 1.4 mm, but it is not ready at the end (top and side video against a mm scale). 0.25: at some moment the triangle tips were within 2.7 mm (5 degrees), however far out the flange stood (close video). Simulation: kept every control step (20 Hz) from the flange's four joints (gap round the joint = distance out along the axis plus 31.5 mm times the sine of its tilt) and from points on every collision face of both grippers, fingers and last wrist links, 3 mm apart; still: joints move under 0.3 mm and 0.3 degrees; an unknown or stale state scores 0. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 1,200 steps per lot (60 s at 20 Hz); two lots
reset_notes: Shut off the air, pull the flange out to its stop square to the housing, turn it to the lot's angle against a printed 75-degree scale held on the housing, then turn the air back on at 1 bar (the flange stays out and the sensor stays tripped). Check the UR3e is braked at the stated joint angles. Acknowledge the controller's sensor stop only after scoring. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: UR3e built from cylinders at its published joint spacing; body sizes and link offsets estimated; braked, so static. CSR50 at datasheet size; its flange moves on four joints (12.5 mm out, two 12.5 deg tilts, free turn). Pressure is a rule: flange seated within 0.8 mm all round and 2.5 deg of its mark for 1 s (estimate) makes it ready and holds it (125 N cap). Off the mark its seat stops it 2.5 mm out (estimate). Seal friction 1.5 N, 0.05 N m (estimates). No air flow simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A and B: 0, 0; both arms lowered toward the bench near their bases and never reached the sensor; 1,200-step limit). Scripted demo: 1.0 (lots A and B: 1.0, 1.0; 300 and 301 steps).
